```{r intro,echo=F,warning=F,message=F}
library(DT)
```

## Introduction

> -   Drafting a permit requires critical flows

> -   Here, we will calculate relevant stream flows for an imaginary facility on Caldwell's Creek near Appomattox, Virginia.

> -   We will pull streamflow data from USGS gages using the **dataRetrieval** R package and run some basic **tidyverse** summary functions.

> -   Optionally, we can join site-specific data to our USGS gage data and scale our flow values to our permitting needs

## Step 1: Look at Site and Nearby Streamgages

::: flexRowMain
::: flexChild50
> -   A <a href="https://www.google.com/maps/place/37%C2%B019'40.9%22N+78%C2%B051'07.3%22W/@37.3238666,-78.8749752,13.21z/data=!4m5!3m4!1s0x0:0x995ab048038a848!8m2!3d37.328024!4d-78.85203">small facility</a> needs their VPDES permit renewed for their 2.5 MGD discharge to Caldwell's Creek.

> -   Concerned with the discharge of Benzene to the creek. The human-health water quality criteria of 160 ug/L is applicable.

> -   We need to know what the *Harmonic Mean* flow of the stream is UPSTREAM of the facility for our RPA. So how can we calculate this?
:::

## Step 2: Download and Investigate Gage Data

Now that we know what gage we want to look at, we need to pull in some data. We can use **dataRetrieval** to get all 100 years of data at once!

We will want to pull daily (USGS code "dv") mean streamflow data (USGS parameter code "00060" and stat code "00003"). You can explore more [parameter](https://help.waterdata.usgs.gov/parameter_cd?group_cd=%) and [stat codes](https://help.waterdata.usgs.gov/code/stat_cd_nm_query?stat_nm_cd=%25&fmt=html) here.

```{r chunk1,eval=F}
#"Date", "Flow", "QC"
names(gageData_all) <-
```

```{r chunk2,eval=FALSE}
#Filter for instances where QC is not "P" (Provisional)
gageData_QC <- gageData_all %>%
```

## Step 2: The Decision

Instead, we will use gage 02064000 which has a more stable flow record (notice that we must filter for "P Ice" as well)

```{r chunk5}
#We will use the dataRetrieval function readNWISdv to get mean daily streamflow
gageData_all <- readNWISdv("02064000",parameterCd = "00060")
#We will set some names for the data frame to make it easier to work with
names(gageData_all) <- c("agency","site_no","Date","Flow","QC")
#Filter for instances where QC is not "P" (Provisional)
gageData_QC <- gageData_all %>% 
  filter(QC != "P", QC != "P Ice")
```

## Step 3: Calculate the Harmonic Mean

Where Q is streamflow, the harmonic mean is computed as:\
$$HM=\frac{1}{\Sigma \frac{1}{Q}}$$

To adjust for any days of zero flow, we can do the following calculation:\
$$HM_u=\Sigma \frac{1}{Q}$$ $$HM=\frac{(N_d-n_z)}{HM_u} * \frac{N_d-n_z}{N_d}$$ Where $N_d$ is the total number of days and $n_z$ is the number of days of zero flow.

## Step 3: Calculate the Harmonic Mean

So, let's start off by first creating a data frame that has all the non-zero flow values and then calculating $N_d$ and $n_z$ (perhaps using the length() or dim() functions)

```{r chunk6,eval = FALSE}
#Let's filter our gageData_QC to only include positive flow values
gageData_noZeros <- gageData_QC %>% 
  
  
#We can use length to determine how many flow entries there are in our complete dataset
N_d <- length()
#We can then calculate the difference between N_d and gageData_noZeroes
n_z <- 

```

## Step 3: Calculate the Harmonic Mean

You should see that at this gage, all flow values are above zero! This makes the harmonic mean calculation easy!

```{r key_chunk7,warning = FALSE, message = FALSE}
#Let's calculate the harmonic mean flow using the formula above:
HM_u <- sum(1 / gageData_noZeros$Flow)
HM <- ((N_d-n_z)/HM_u) * ((N_d-n_z) / N_d)
HM
```

The harmonic mean flow is about `r round(HM,1)` cfs at this gage!

## Step 4: Scaling the Stream Flows

> -   We calculated the harmonic mean at the USGS gage on Falling River, but our site is nearly 15 miles upstream!

> -   We can scale the flow using streamflow data collected at our facility, on-and-off, for the past 20 years

> -   A regression of the USGS gage streamflow and upstream flow at our facility will be the key to getting our permitted flow values

## Step 4A: Fixing the Dates

The operator entered the dates using abbreviations. How can we fix this?

as.Date()! Check out the format section under the help menu. You will need to enter a custom format using strptime. See the help menu for strptime or this [link](https://www.stat.berkeley.edu/~s133/dates.html). There are a few hints below if you find yourself stuck. Dates are tricky!

```{r chunk10,eval = FALSE}
#We need to make sure R knows there are dates here
facilityFlow$Date <- as.Date(facilityFlow$Date)
#For the discharge data, the dates are in the format 01-Jan-21 to represent
#January 1, 2021. We need to make sure R looks for this custom format using
#the strptime helpers
facilityDis_long$Date <-
```

## Step 4A: Fixing the Dates {.build}

*Hint 1:* The standard R date format is %Y-%m-%d, representing a date in the format YYYY-mm-dd. We can use %d to represent the day, but we need to find the code for the abbreviated month and the two-digit year.

*Hint 2:* You will need %d to represent the days, %b to represent the abbreviated month, and %y to represent the two-digit year

::: reducedBotMargin
```{r key_chunk10,warning = FALSE, message = FALSE}
#We need to make sure R knows there are dates here
facilityFlow$Date <- as.Date(facilityFlow$Date)
#For the discharge data, the dates are in the format 01-Jan-21 to represent
#January 1, 2021. We need to make sure R looks for this custom format 
facilityDis_long$Date <- as.Date(facilityDis_long$Date,format = "%d-%b-%y")

facilityDis_long$Date[1];class(facilityDis_long$Date)
```
:::

## Step 4B: Determine Upstream Flow

We have the flow downstream of our facility and the discharge from the facility, but we need the flow upstream of the discharge (so the streamflow that excludes the discharge flow!).

We will need to convert that flow into CFS (1 MGD = 1.547229 CFS)!

```{r key_chunk11_key,message = FALSE, error = FALSE}
#Lets create a data frame to store our flow upstream of our facility. It will
#have all of the dates in facilityFlow
upstreamFlow <- facilityFlow
#Subtract the discharge from the facility from the flow downstream of our facility 
upstreamFlow$FlowMGD <- upstreamFlow$FlowMGD - facilityDis_long$FlowMGD
#Convert to cfs!
upstreamFlow <- upstreamFlow %>% 
  mutate(FlowCFS = FlowMGD * 1000000 * 231 / 12 / 12 / 12 / 3600 / 24)
```

## Step 4B: Join and Compare Flows

Using *inner_join()*, we can create a data frame that has all of the flow values that occurred on dates that are present in **both** *upstreamFlow* and *gageData_QC*

::: columns-2
```{r chunk12_key,warning=FALSE,message=FALSE}

#We only want to keep dates that are in
#both the gage data and our facility
#data. Plus we will want to rename the
#columns to something more meaningful
flowComparison <- upstreamFlow %>% 
  ###<b>
  inner_join(gageData_QC,
             by = "Date") %>% 
  ###</b>

         UpstreamFlow = FlowCFS,
         GageFlow = Flow)
```

## Step 4B: Conduct a NLS Regression

```{r chunk14,message = FALSE, warning = FALSE}
#We can use nls to determine a relationship between GageFlow and UpstreamFlow
#by providing it a formula and initial guesses
NLR <- nls(data = flowComparison,
           formula = UpstreamFlow ~ A * GageFlow ^ B,
           start = c(A = 1,B = 1))
#Using summary(), we can learn more about our regression
summary(NLR)
```

## Step 4B: Create a Flow Prediction Function

We can turn our NLS object into a function to predict flow! Again, this is pretty advanced but it shows how easy custom functions are to work with!

```{r chunk14_continued,message = FALSE, warning = FALSE}
#We create a function out of our regression called regFun to estimate flow at our
#site based on a USGS flow
regFun <- function(GageFlow,NLR){
  coeffA <- coef(NLR)[[1]]
  coeffB <- coef(NLR)[[2]]

  Qupstream <- coeffA * GageFlow ^ coeffB
  return(Qupstream)
}

#Test regFun for yourself:
###<b>
regFun(300,NLR)
###</b>
```

## Step 4B: Calculate the Final Harmonic Mean

We built a custom function, regFun, that uses a non-linear regression to predict flow upstream of our facility.

Let's include it on our plot and finally use it to calculate the Harmonic Mean upstream of our facility.

